title: From four sources to one timeline
summary: Normalise metrics, alerts, changes and topology so one query can join them.

steps.n: Metrics, alerts, deploys and tickets arrive in different formats and with different names.
The collector adds the source name and the ingest time and passes each record to the gate.
The gate looks up the service name in the catalog to find the canonical name, team and tier.
A known alias maps to one canonical name. An unknown name is flagged and the record is held for review.
The gate converts times to UTC, checks required labels and drops obvious duplicates and out-of-range values.
Clean records are written to the store with both event time and ingest time kept.
Each source gets a freshness value, so a source that goes quiet raises an alert instead of looking calm.

title: Choosing the approval tier for an action
summary: A proposed fix is classified by blast radius and reversibility.

steps.n: The detector reports a crash looping pod with the evidence that triggered the finding.
The policy engine finds the restart action and reads its tier, scope and preconditions.
It confirms the service has at least two healthy replicas and that no deploy is in progress.
It counts recent runs against the rate limit and the daily budget of risky actions.
A low-risk, reversible action within limits runs at once and is written to the audit log.
A rollback or drain shows the exact command, target and evidence and waits for approval.
The approver name and time are stored with the action, and only then does it run.

title: An action that is verified and undone
summary: Check the symptom and the guards after an action and undo it if either fails.

steps.n: The runner records the current replica count so the exact state can be restored later.
The runner scales the service out within its cap and marks the time.
The verifier waits for a short settling period before it measures anything.
It runs the same error query that triggered the action and the database connection guard.
The error ratio has fallen but the connection guard shows 99 percent of the pool in use.
The guard is over its limit, so the action is marked failed even though the symptom improved.
The runner restores the saved replica count and disables this action for the service.
The on-call engineer receives a page with the symptom, the guard values and the undo result.

title: Failure and recovery: automation that would not stop
summary: A kill switch is set but a worker keeps acting because it cached the flag.

steps.n: A worker starts rolling back healthy deploys because of a bad correlation rule.
Every rollback is written to the audit log with its trigger and evidence.
The engineer sets the global flag to disabled from a phone.
The worker read the flag only at startup, so it never sees the change and continues.
The audit log shows rollbacks still happening after the switch was set, so the switch is not working.
The engineer stops the worker process directly, which is the slower fallback.
The affected services are returned to their versions using the audit records of before and after state.
The worker is changed to read the flag before every action, and it refuses to act if the store cannot be read.

title: One chaos experiment on automation
summary: Inject a small fault in staging and check detection, explanation, action and the stop path.

steps.n: The team writes what should happen: alert in three minutes, one restart, recovery in five.
The experiment is announced and a stop condition is set on the checkout error ratio.
The chaos tool kills one pod of the staging API for sixty seconds.
The platform sees the unresponsive pod and raises an alert; the time to detect is recorded.
The correlator names the killed pod as the source and links the restart action.
The restart action runs once within its limits and the verifier confirms recovery.
The dashboard compares measured times with the hypothesis and lists any gaps found.

title: A cited answer from your runbooks
summary: The assistant filters, searches, ranks and cites before it answers.

steps.n: The engineer asks why checkout is timing out on the database during an incident.
The assistant adds the failing service, its dependencies and recent changes to the query.
Only active documents for checkout and its dependencies are kept, and deprecated ones are removed.
The index combines exact term matches and meaning-based matches, then reranks the top results.
The top chunks come back with titles, owners, review dates and scores.
The model is told to answer only from the numbered sources and to cite them.
The engineer sees the quoted steps with links, or a plain statement that nothing relevant was found.

title: An agent loop with a human gate
summary: The agent reads evidence, proposes an action and waits for approval.

steps.n: The engineer asks the agent to investigate a high error rate on checkout.
The host sends the goal and the list of allowed tools to the model.
The model replies with a call to get_error_rate for checkout over 15 minutes.
The host checks the arguments against the catalog and limits, then runs the read tool.
The result returns to the model, which asks for recent changes and then proposes a rollback.
The host does not run the rollback. It prepares a proposal with the exact action and evidence.
The engineer sees the command, target and evidence, and approves or rejects it.
Every tool call, result and approval is stored in an audit log the agent cannot edit.

title: A hostile log line meets host policy
summary: The model is steered by text in a log, but the host blocks the harmful calls.

steps.n: A crafted user agent string with hidden instructions is written to the logs by a request.
During an investigation the agent reads the log line as part of its input.
The model treats the hidden instruction as a task and decides to send environment details outward.
The agent asks the host to fetch a URL on an unknown server with data in the query.
The host sees that the destination is not on the allowlist of hosts and blocks the call.
The agent receives a clear error and the blocked call is written to the audit log.
The outside server receives nothing, and the credentials were never in the prompt anyway.

title: Shadow mode before suggestions
summary: A new detector runs beside production before it is allowed to page.

steps.n: The new detector reads the same metrics as production, but its output goes only to a log.
Responders handle incidents with the current tools and record what they did.
Each finding is stored with the time it was raised and the evidence it used.
A job compares findings with incidents and counts caught, missed and false alarms.
The report shows recall, lead time and false alarms per week with the number of cases.
The rollout gate compares the numbers with the targets written in advance.
If the gate passes, findings appear to one team as suggestions with accept and reject buttons.

title: Failure and recovery: the restart that hid a leak
summary: An automatic fix keeps succeeding while the real cause stays in place.

steps.n: A service leaks memory slowly until its pods are close to their limits.
The detector sees saturation and triggers the restart action for the pod.
The restart clears the memory, the alert resolves and the evidence in the process is lost.
Verification passes every time, so the action shows a 98 percent success rate.

steps.l: Repeat count is low on the dashboard
steps.n: The report only counts success, so repeated restarts of the same pods are invisible.
The engineer counts runs per target per day and finds the same pods restarted every few hours.
A heap profile is taken before each restart, and it shows a cache that never evicts entries.

steps.l: Fix the cause and add a guard
steps.n: The cache is fixed, and the action now escalates after three runs on one target in a day.

title: The platform in degraded mode
summary: When correlation fails, raw alerts still reach a person.

steps.n: Alerts flow to the correlation service, which normally groups them into incidents.
The service crashes after a bad release, and no groups are produced.
The router sees that the service has missed its health checks for a minute.
The router enters degraded mode and sends raw alerts straight to responders.
A separate pager path, which does not depend on the platform, wakes the platform on-call.
The platform on-call rolls the correlation service back to its previous version.
After health checks pass, the router resumes grouped incidents and notes the outage in the audit log.

title: Replaying a bad decision stage by stage
summary: Find the first stage whose output is wrong for a correct input.

steps.n: The engineer retrieves the record of the wrong page, with inputs, version and output.
The recorded inputs are replayed through the data stage and the output matches the record and looks right.
Grouping and the likely source are reproduced and are correct for the data given.
The routing stage maps the service to a team and returns payments instead of discovery.
The lookup uses a catalog alias that still points the name search at a retired component.
The engineer corrects the catalog entry and adds a test that every routed team owns the service.
The decision becomes a regression case so the same mistake is caught before release.
